project.title: The Living Herbal
project.subtitle: Three early herbals, newly readable
project.method: Mistral OCR 4 paragraph geometry, conservative English reading layers, and non-generative source artwork

books.title: De Historia Stirpivm Commentarii Insignes
books.subtitle: A modern English reading facsimile
books.creator: Leonhart Fuchs
books.description: Fuchs pairs a systematic Latin account of plants with some of the Renaissance's most influential botanical woodcuts. The English layer keeps the page architecture while opening the text to non-Latin readers.
books.significance: A landmark of descriptive botany and botanical illustration, first printed in 1542 with more than five hundred plant images.

books.title: Herbarius zü Teütsch
books.subtitle: A modern English reading facsimile
books.creator: Attributed to Johannes von Cuba; printed by Hans Schönsperger
books.description: This vernacular incunable combines dense two-column blackletter with compact botanical woodcuts, many touched with color. The facsimile translates the early German while preserving the irregular printed grid.
books.significance: An early German-language herbal in the Gart der Gesundheit tradition and a demanding example of incunable page design.

books.title: A Boke of the Propreties of Herbes
books.subtitle: A normalized modern-English reading facsimile
books.creator: Anonymous; 1552 Copland/Kele imprint
books.description: A compact descendant of the first herbal printed in English. Its heavy blackletter and unfamiliar spelling become readable modern English without smoothing away the work's abrupt recipes or period voice.
books.significance: The anonymous Banckes tradition begins with the first printed English herbal of 1525; this complete 1552 imprint ends with its original colophon.
